correctness.rationale: For n=2, K_2=2-I with I=1{X1=X2}. Exact conditioning yields E[I]=s_2, E[M_2]=1-2s_2+s_3, E[I M_2]=s_2-s_3; hence Cov(K_2,M_2)=(1+s_2)s_3-2s_2^2. For fixed feasible s_2, compactness allows maximizing s_3 over nonnegative m-tuples; active-support Lagrange equations yield at most two positive masses. If two coordinates share the larger mass a>b, tangent vector e_i-e_j annihilates both first constraints while the constrained Hessian is strictly positive 6(a-b) in each coordinate, contradicting maximality. Thus each nonuniform maximizer has one large mass, equal smaller ones; zero entries mean smaller active support. For r=2,3,4 the exact covariance factors are -2b^2(1-b)^2, -2b^2(18b^3-12b^2+1), -6b^3(48b^2-30b+5), respectively, all strictly negative on 0<b<=1/r (r=3 bracket >=1/3, r=4 discriminant -60). Uniform support r>=2 gives -(r-1)/r^3. One atom gives zero. The positive five-atom rational vector (4/5,1/20,1/20,1/20,1/20) yields exactly 1/1600; epsilon continuity gives any larger full finite support, while uniform laws give negative covariance. Independent direct sample-space enumeration of 9,948 all-positive integer-composition laws (d<=6, denominator <=15), symbolic one-heavy polynomial factorization and full tree SHA reconstruction corroborate the stated proof; finite cases alone are not its unrestricted justification.

value.rationale: For fixed-sample species discovery, observed richness and total unseen population probability are basic nonredundant statistics. The theorem resolves a natural exact minimal-alphabet sign question at n=2, the first sample size with nonconstant K_n: support<=4 forces negative covariance but heterogeneity from five atoms onward allows positive covariance. It is a complete possibility classification over all finite support sizes, and clarifies why independent Poissonization masks the sign reversal. The witness and proof are not arbitrary parameter slices or known-table recomputations. The precise cutoff could be useful when analyzing the dependence of sample coverage and diversity at short horizons.
